input: Take a welding taster class at a local workshop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Welding covers several techniques (MIG, TIG, stick, oxy-acetylene) — knowing which type they want to try changes which classes to look for.
Their city or region determines which local workshops, makerspaces, or colleges are actually available to them.
Whether they need a class on a weekend, weekday evening, or have a specific date deadline affects which options are viable.
Taster class prices range from free community events to £100+ paid courses — budget sets a hard filter on options.
Going alone vs. with a friend or group affects logistics, whether a private booking is needed, and group-discount relevance.
Knowing whether the goal is pure curiosity, a step toward a hobby, or a vocational skill changes how much depth the class needs to deliver.
Identifying the very next action — searching online, calling a local makerspace, asking for a recommendation — determines how to kick off the plan immediately.

gold.taskTitle: Take a local welding taster class
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to attend a beginner welding taster session at a workshop or makerspace near them.

questions.title: Which welding technique do you want to try first?
questions.description: Identify whether the user is interested in a specific method such as MIG, TIG, stick (arc), or has no preference and wants a general introduction.

questions.title: What city or area should the workshop be near?
questions.description: Establish the user's location so that only genuinely local venues and providers are surfaced in the plan.

questions.title: Do you have a target date or timeframe to complete this?
questions.description: Find out if there is a deadline, an ideal month, or a specific day-of-week preference that would filter available class schedules.

questions.title: What is the most you are willing to spend on the class?
questions.description: Capture a budget ceiling so the plan can focus on free community events, affordable makerspace sessions, or paid professional courses accordingly.

questions.title: Will you be attending alone or bringing someone with you?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo booking or a shared experience, which affects whether a private group session or a standard open class is more appropriate.

questions.title: What is the main reason you want to try welding?
questions.description: Understand the underlying motivation — casual curiosity, a potential new hobby, a specific project need, or a career interest — so the class depth and follow-up steps match the goal.

questions.title: Have you already found any venues, or starting from scratch?
questions.description: Establish whether the user has already researched options or needs the plan to begin from the very first discovery step, such as searching directories or contacting makerspaces.
